title: The Institutional Will
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: An institutional will is a coordinated set of decisions about authority, access, assets, archives, obligations, interpretation, privacy, and care—not a substitute for legal estate or corporate instruments.
An accession-quality record preserves a house object beyond the founder’s lifetime while keeping the object, maker attribution, and museum stewardship distinct.

01 · INTENT — What should happen—and why?. Write desired outcomes for company, name, work in progress, archive, public voice, teaching, licensing, philanthropy, privacy, dependents, and closure in plain language.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · AUTHORITY — Which instrument can make it happen?. Map corporate documents, contracts, employment terms, IP records, wills or trusts, powers, beneficiary designations, data policies, archive agreements, and jurisdiction-specific requirements with counsel.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · STEWARD — Who acts, who substitutes, who reviews?. Name primary and alternate decision-makers by function; address conflicts, expertise, compensation, access, accountability, dissent, cultural authority, and removal.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · REHEARSE — Does the plan work in practice?. Run incapacity, death, departure, sale, closure, dispute, data loss, platform failure, preservation emergency, and public controversy; record fixes and review dates.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Write a one-page plain-language intent letter.
Attach every asset and authority to its governing record or mark unresolved.
Name stewards, alternates, conflicts, funding, and review.
Take the map to estate, corporate, IP, employment, privacy, tax, and cultural advisers as relevant.
